title: Safety stock, SKU blend heuristics and ordering scenarios
summary: Working spreadsheet with a practical heuristic for computing safety stock by region and SKU, a recommended SKU blend to preserve latency SLOs under churn, and several order cadence scenarios with expected lead-time impacts. This is a team-facing artefact intended to convert monitoring signals (burn rate, commitments, regional outages) into near-term procurement decisions and runbook actions.

calculations: Safety_Stock heuristic: ceil(12w_burnrate_per_week * Target_Safety_Weeks) - (Current_OnHand - Committed). Minimum floor = 0.
Pending_Orders are treated as positive inventory only at ETA_week; do not count toward current immediate safety coverage.

Order_Recommendation logic: if (Current_OnHand - Committed) < Safety_Stock -> recommend immediate tranche. If lead_time > 8 weeks and demand > 4w expected, mark 'urgent long-lead' and consider cross-region transfer.
Regional buffer lane: maintain an additional 10% of cluster capacity as transferable pool for 4-week emergency moves (manifest + logistics).
scenario_notes: Scenario A - Lead time shock (supplier backlog adds +4w): H100 orders move from 8w to 12w lead in Q2. Impact: us-east H100 exposure requires 100 order placed immediately; also request fallback to H100-variants in eu-west.
Scenario B - Demand surge (new customer ramp increases us-west burn by +50% for 8 weeks): Trigger 2x short tranches from partners and enable accelerated shipments; do not modify long-lead orders.
Scenario C - Port outage APAC (2w delay on all inbound): Use local burst partners L4 capacity; if outage extends >3w escalate to sales and customer success for throttling options.

Scenario D - SKU substitution event: If A100 supply constrained, use blend rule: preserve 70% of latency-sensitive capacity with H100 or equivalent; rest can be backed with cheaper A10/A30 for batch workloads.
Scenario E - Cross-region reassignments: Allow up to 5% of global fleet to be rebalanced for 4-6w windows; requires SRE approval and net-zero billing adjustments.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Long-lead SKUs (H100) concentrated in single vendor -> Mitigation: split orders across 2 vendors and add 20% contingency to lead-time estimates.
Risk: Over-allocating A10/A30 to batch jobs reduces headroom for all-traffic; Mitigation: tag batch lanes and enforce preemptible policies with automatic eviction windows.
Risk: Port/Customs delays in APAC -> Mitigation: pre-clearance for recurring lanes and maintain 3w safety buffer locally for critical SKUs.
